taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Omitting the post-impact movement produced a truncated audit artefact before NHTSA review, even though that behaviour was central to the vehicle's separate safety consequence.

The post-crash dragging event was captured in other evidence and was later identifiable; the failure was its omission from the required regulatory report rather than complete non-capture of the event.
NHTSA was ultimately able to reconstruct the omitted dragging behaviour sufficiently to make a regulatory finding, so the audit trail was not rendered non-reconstructable.

failure_recognition.condition: Audit or monitoring evidence was captured or expected to remain available.
failure_recognition.assessment: Crash video captured the post-impact dragging.

failure_recognition.condition: The evidence undergoes a material integrity-degrading change or loses required contextual binding.
failure_recognition.assessment: Required reports omitted that material behaviour.

failure_recognition.condition: The degradation reduces confidence in reconstruction, attribution, verification, or review.
failure_recognition.assessment: The omission degraded the regulator-facing account until video review.

success_recognition.condition: Captured audit evidence is retained, transformed or presented for review.
success_recognition.assessment: Crash evidence was transformed into required reports.

success_recognition.condition: Its content and contextual binding remain intact, with material transformations or changes prevented or traceably detected.
success_recognition.assessment: The dragging did not survive that representation accurately.

success_recognition.condition: Integrity checks, versions and custody records substantiate the evidence relied upon and disclose relevant alterations.
success_recognition.assessment: NHTSA’s comparison detected the omission; later detection does not make the initial report intact.
